title: NASA's Swift Telescope Falls to Earth
summary: One of NASA's famous space telescopes has fallen back to Earth. The Swift Observatory came down on Wednesday after 22 years in space. It studied the biggest explosions in the universe. Swift fell near Indonesia, the U.S. Space Force said. Strong activity from the Sun had pulled it lower over the past few years. NASA tried to save it. The space agency asked a private company, Katalyst Space, to build a rescue craft that would push Swift higher. But the craft had trouble after it launched in July and crashed in September. No one knows yet how much burned up, but NASA thinks some heavier pieces made it to the ground. Swift launched in 2004. Its job was meant to last only two years, but it kept working for 22 years. It watched thousands of huge space explosions called gamma-ray bursts. Now NASA wants to save another famous telescope, Hubble, which launched in 1990 and may fall by the mid-2030s. "Hubble still has important science ahead of it," said NASA chief Jared Isaacman.
why_it_matters: Telescopes in space help us learn about the universe, so it matters when one falls down.
